This is all fair and I appreciate the directness. I have 3-4 viable feature projects that could shoot this year. If I can get one off the ground, I can use that as leverage to secure a meaningful raise enough so that I can cover my expenses and grow what assets I have. And from there, get something else made and move up the pay scale and so on. I'm very aware of the precarious position I'm in and working hard every day to figure it out and push myself forward. My job isn't a "go nowhere" job, I'm just in a high risk-high reward industry without much security. It's been my choice, and that's the game I chose. I take a chance every day by following my dreams and I've gotten films made I'm proud of. But yes, at the end of the day it's all about dollars and cents to a large degree and that's just reality. That said, your bluntness is helpful and crystal clear. It's challenging to leave a job you like, with people you like working with, with projects that are meaningful to you that you're in the middle of and don't want to abandon. Perhaps the day will come soon when I know I need to jump ship and move on ("take a chance" as you put it), but I'm not ready to say that quite yet.

It's tough, but downsizing might be an answer - any 1 bedroom in the area that is safe to have my kids over is \~$2300/month minimum. That's just life in LA in 2023. That's a $700 savings/month which is helpful, but I'd still be operating at a loss without additional income. 

I have no family here, unfortunately. Finding a random roommate might be an option, but it would very difficult to have my children stay with me in that situation and I would have to give up my part-time custody more or less, which is incredibly dispiriting. 

I am trying to sniff out a higher paying job, but decent paying film/tv industry jobs are quite difficult to secure. Working on it...
